title: Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Clinical Outcomes After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Using the ATTUNE™ Knee System with Patient-Specific Alignment (PSA) and VELYS™ Robotic-Assisted Surgical Technique Versus Mechanical Alignment (MA) with Conventional Manual Surgical Technique
summary:
Background
In advanced wear of the knee joint, complete replacement with an artificial knee joint may become necessary. The surgical method that has been used successfully for several decades positions the artificial knee joint according to fixed, standardized axes. Extensive registry data and good long-term results are available for this method, with low rates of further surgery. Nevertheless, approximately 15 to 20 percent of patients are not fully satisfied after the procedure or continue to experience pain and functional limitations.
Over the past 15 years, more individually tailored surgical methods have increasingly been used. In these procedures, the position of the artificial knee joint is adapted more closely to the individual shape of the leg, the natural joint line, and the tension of the knee ligaments. Robotic-assisted surgical support is intended to implement this individual planning with greater precision. It is assumed that this may result in more natural knee function and higher patient satisfaction. However, only a limited number of studies have directly compared both surgical methods in a systematic manner, over a longer period, and using clinical assessments, imaging, and objective movement data.

Research question
This study investigates whether an individually tailored, Robotic-assisted implantation of an artificial knee joint leads to better outcomes than conventional manual surgery with standardized alignment.
The comparison focuses in particular on pain, function in daily life, range of motion, satisfaction, gait, physical activity, restoration of leg alignment, and the occurrence of complications and further surgery.

Methods
The study involves 300 patients who are scheduled to undergo their first total knee replacement. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups in a blinded manner. This means that patients do not know which intervention group they are in or how they will be operated on. Unblinding may occur at any time upon the patient’s explicit request; at the latest, this will take place after the completion of the final follow-up examination 12 months postoperatively.
In the first group, the artificial knee joint is implanted with the support of a robotic-assisted surgical system. The alignment is adapted as closely as possible to the individual shape of the leg, the natural joint line, and the tension of the knee ligaments.
In the control group, the operation is performed using conventional manual instruments. The artificial knee joint is positioned according to standardized axes. The same model of artificial knee joint is used in both groups.
Assessments are carried out approximately six weeks before surgery and at three and twelve months after surgery. Pain, everyday function, quality of life, and satisfaction are assessed using standardized questionnaires. In addition, the range of motion and stability of the knee joint are examined by a physician. Gait, physical activity, and loading of the legs are assessed using wearable movement sensors, video recordings during walking, and pressure-sensing insoles. During surgery, data on the alignment and positioning of the artificial knee joint are also recorded.
Only X-ray images that are already obtained as part of routine medical care are evaluated for the study. No additional X-ray examinations or invasive procedures are planned. The individual follow-up period is twelve months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for primary total knee arthroplasty using the ATTUNE™ Knee System with a Medial Stabilized (MS) insert
Symptomatic knee osteoarthritis after unsuccessful conservative treatment
Fulfilment of the applicable indication criteria for total knee arthroplasty
Age ≥ 18 years
American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification 1–3
Sufficient German language proficiency
Written informed consent to participate in the study
Written informed consent for the processing of study-related data
Exclusion criteria:
Valgus alignment with an aHKA > +2° (positive aHKA values indicate valgus alignment, whereas negative values indicate varus alignment); this corresponds to the exclusion of CPAK types 3, 6, and 9.
Known allergy to nickel, cobalt, or chromium
Impaired legal capacity
American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification 4 or 5
Care dependency level 3 or higher
Subsequent withdrawal of consent to randomization or refusal of the assigned surgical procedure
